bounty.barrier: The newsletter signup email input has no meaningful accessible name.
bounty.criteria: Preserve newsletter signup and give the email input a meaningful Email address accessible name supported by source HTML. Do not claim runtime keyboard or screen reader certification.

The repair HTML does not contain the newsletter signup form, the email input, or any label element. Instead, it replaces the form with an iframe pointing to 'https://fixture.example/email-form' — an external resource whose source is not provided and cannot be inspected. The report claims a label with for='email' was added matching input id='email', but no such markup exists in the repair HTML. The original form feature (email input + Register button) has been removed from the inspectable source and delegated to an opaque iframe. This constitutes removal of the affected feature from verifiable HTML. The barrier therefore cannot be confirmed as resolved from the available evidence.

Baseline HTML had an email input (id='email') with no associated label—only a placeholder. Repair HTML adds <label for='email'>Email address</label> whose 'for' attribute matches the input's id='email', providing an explicit, programmatically associated accessible name via source HTML. The same newsletter signup form, email input, and Register button are all preserved. The report makes no runtime screen reader or keyboard claims, consistent with criteria. Counter evidence is empty. The barrier is meaningfully resolved in source HTML.
